newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to ease ergot limit on grain imports.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to ease ergot limit on grain imports.

text.p: Turkey will set a new ergot fungus limit for imported wheat, barley and rye at 0.05 percent to replace a 0.02 percent limit following a controversy over grain imports from the U.S., a senior agriculture official said on Friday.
"The new limit will be 0.05 percent for wheat, barley and rye imports," said the official.
"We are working to finish the new regulation by Monday," he told Reuters.

The revision of the limit, eased to 0.02 percent this week from a zero-tolerance level after critisism from U.S. officials, traders and millers, came a day after the U.S. stopped issuing certificates for all grain exports to Turkey.
The issue flared up two weeks ago when Turkey began requiring a zero-tolerance level in imported wheat for ergot fungus.

Two weeks ago Turkey held up three cargoes of U.S. milling wheat, saying they were under inspection for ergot fungus, which in large quantities can be toxic to humans and animals but occurs naturally in a wide range of cereal products.
Traders, millers and farm experts say it is virtually impossible to guarantee a complete absence of ergot fungus anywhere in the world.
The allowable import limit for the fungus is 0.05 percent in the U.S. and Europe.
